title: Apoorva Mukhija Reveals She Felt Suicidal During India's Got Latent Controversy
excerpt: The content creator opened up about her mental health struggles on Lock Upp, crediting friend Sufi Motiwala with saving her life during the fallout from the controversial YouTube show.
body:
• Apoorva Mukhija told fellow Lock Upp contestant Sufi Motiwala that she would have "killed myself" without his support during the India's Got Latent fallout.
  • The February 2025 controversy saw Mukhija receive death threats, rape threats, and acid-attack warnings after a vulgar segment on Samay Raina's YouTube show went viral.
  • The emotional reunion on Lock Upp Season 2 reignited public debate about the toll of online harassment on India's young creators.
  • Mukhija has since rebuilt her career with appearances on The Traitors and a Bollywood debut in Nadaaniyan.

Content creator Apoorva Mukhija, known online as "The Rebel Kid," has revealed she experienced suicidal thoughts during the aftermath of the India's Got Latent controversy in early 2025. The disclosure came during an emotional moment on Netflix's Lock Upp Season 2, where Mukhija entered as a wildcard contestant and reunited with former close friend Sufi Motiwala.

"I would've killed myself if, at the time of the Latent fiasco, if I hadn't had Sufi," Mukhija told Motiwala during their on-camera reunion, according to Zoom TV. She added: "You saved my life; I genuinely wouldn't have been able to survive Latent if it wasn't for you."

"You saved my life; I genuinely wouldn't have been able to survive Latent if it wasn't for you."

— Apoorva Mukhija, on Lock Upp Season 2

What Was the India's Got Latent Controversy?

The crisis traces back to February 2025, when a segment on comedian Samay Raina's YouTube show India's Got Latent went viral for all the wrong reasons. During the episode, guest judge and podcaster Ranveer Allahbadia posed an explicit hypothetical question to a contestant that was widely condemned as vulgar and obscene. Mukhija, Raina, Ashish Chanchlani, and others appeared as panelists on the episode.

https://x.com/NewsX/status/2080627897845665901

The backlash was immediate and severe. Multiple FIRs were filed across states — Assam Police acted first, followed by Mumbai Police. The Maharashtra Women's Commission and the National Commission for Women summoned the participants. By February 12, 2025, Raina had deleted all India's Got Latent episodes from YouTube and pledged full cooperation with investigating agencies.

Politicians weighed in sharply. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis commented on the need for accountability, while Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma confirmed that Guwahati police had filed an FIR against the individuals involved.

The Personal Toll on Mukhija

For Mukhija, the professional fallout quickly turned into a personal nightmare. She reported receiving threats of rape, acid attacks, and death on her social media accounts. A far-right Hindu outfit in Gwalior declared a bounty of ₹1 lakh to cut off Allahbadia's tongue, and the Karni Sena warned that Mukhija would be physically assaulted if she attended the IIFA Awards in Jaipur — leading organisers to drop her from the guest list.

The 23-year-old was also forced to move out of her Mumbai apartment after police visits and was dropped by several brand partners. In a video titled Till I Say It Is, released months later, she addressed the harassment publicly for the first time. "I should have been more mindful, and I truly have learned my lesson," she said, while also describing the moment on the show as a reaction born from "genuine anger and the need to retaliate."

Mukhija also shared screenshots of threatening messages on Instagram, captioning the post: "And that's not even 1%."

A Friendship Broken and Rebuilt

Mukhija and Motiwala became close during their time on Amazon Prime Video's The Traitors in 2025. But their friendship fractured publicly in the months that followed. Motiwala posted a lengthy statement on Instagram titled "NO MORE LIES," saying he had distanced himself due to a "lack of accountability" and online abuse from Mukhija's followers. He unfollowed her on Instagram, and the two stopped interacting publicly.

Their reunion on Lock Upp — which premiered on Netflix on June 27, 2026, and is hosted by Farah Khan and Riteish Deshmukh — came as a surprise. Motiwala reciprocated Mukhija's sentiment, telling her: "That one year was the most favourite year of my life when we were friends. I genuinely missed you a lot."

"That one year was the most favourite year of my life when we were friends. I genuinely missed you a lot."

— Sufi Motiwala, Lock Upp Season 2

Online Harassment and India's Creator Economy

Mukhija's disclosure adds to a growing body of testimony from Indian content creators about the mental health costs of public controversy. Ranked No. 8 on Forbes India's Top 100 Digital Stars list for 2024, Mukhija commands over four million Instagram followers and has worked with brands including Nike, Netflix, Amazon, Google, and Meta. Yet none of that insulated her from the mob-like response that followed the India's Got Latent episode.

The case also underscores how quickly Indian internet culture can pivot from entertainment to outrage. What began as a provocative comedy segment triggered police action across multiple states, political grandstanding, and sustained harassment campaigns — a pattern that has repeated itself across India's digital landscape with increasing frequency.

What Lies Ahead

Mukhija's career has continued to grow despite the controversy. She appeared on The Traitors and landed a Bollywood debut in Nadaaniyan alongside Khushi Kapoor and Ibrahim Ali Khan. Her entry into Lock Upp Season 2 as a wildcard has already generated headlines, with expected confrontations with fellow contestants Shreya Kalra and the now-eliminated Motiwala.

In a Pinkvilla interview earlier this year, Mukhija said she had moved past the trauma. "I think I am glad I went through that," she said. "I really needed a reality check that Instagram, comments, views are not everything. You are your own person irrespective of what the internet thinks about you."
